title: What is Scientific Research  for Innovation Management?
section: Everything start with a good research question
text:
Everything start with a good research question







1 Descriptive (What, When, Where, Who or How)
e.g. What percentageof coachees report that coaching helped them with a problem they experienced
2 Explanatory (Why?)
e.g. Why dis 65% of coachees report that coacing helped them with a problem they experienced? this





Source: Rojon, C. & Saunders, M. N. K. Formulating a convincing rationale for a research study. Coaching: An International Journal of Theory, Research and Practice 5, 55–61 (2012).

title: What is Scientific Research  for Innovation Management?
text:
Good research question: Descriptive & Explanatory
Being able to provide meaningful explanations requires answers to why (i.e. explanatory) questions in addition to what (i.e. descriptive) questions.
For example:

‘How effective is the coaching process at helping coachees to solve a problem they experience and what are the reasons for this?’
‘To what extent is the coaching process effective at helping coachees solve a problem and why?’



Source: Rojon, C. & Saunders, M. N. K. Formulating a convincing rationale for a research study. Coaching: An International Journal of Theory, Research and Practice 5, 55–61 (2012).

title: What is Scientific Research  for Innovation Management?
section: Mental model when reading an abstract
text:
Mental model when reading an abstract


🌍 Topic → the writer provides background factual information.
⚠️ Problem → The writer presents the gap/problem to treat
🔎 Research Gap → the writer states the limits of current knowledge.
🎯 The purpose : the writer presents the general aim and the specific aim of the study.
📜 Methodology → the writer summarises the methodology and provides details.
📊 Results → the writer indicates the achievement of the study.
🚀 Perspectives → the writer presents the implications of the study.

Report on your literature findings and beware of:

Purposely misrepresenting the work of other authors.


Plagiarism – the use of another’s original words, arguments, or ideas as though they were your own, even if this is done in good faith, out of carelessness, or out of ignorance.

Conclusions → Summary of results and importance of results given the context.

title: Act II: Literature review
section: Mental model when reading an abstract
text:
Mental model when reading an abstract


🌍 Topic → the writer provides background factual information.
⚠️ Problem → The writer presents the gap/problem to treat
🔎 Research Gap → the writer states the limits of current knowledge.
🎯 The purpose : the writer presents the general aim and the specific aim of the study.
📜 Methodology → the writer summarises the methodology and provides details.
📊 Results → the writer indicates the achievement of the study.
🚀 Perspectives → the writer presents the implications of the study.
